templates.title: Template library
templates.howTitle: How to add a template without code
templates.howBody: Open any invitation in the editor, design it the way you like — sections, colors, fonts and images — then press “Save as template” in the top bar. Or press “Create template” at the top of this page to start an empty template from the sections available in the editor. The template shows up here immediately and is available for every new invitation. Personal data is not copied into the template.
templates.importTitle: Import a ready-made template (HTML or ZIP)
templates.importBody: Upload an .html file or a .zip archive containing index.html with its images and local CSS and JavaScript files. Each main element of the page becomes a section you can reorder, hide and edit in the editor, and its styles stay scoped to the section so the rest of the invitation isn't affected.
templates.importLimits: Know the limits: local JavaScript files inside the archive run in the public preview and the published page, while external CDN links are not copied automatically. Upload templates only from a trusted source because JavaScript runs inside the invitation page. An imported template has no ready-made fields such as “bride's name” or “date”; you edit the text and styles directly.

templateNew.title: Create a new template
templateNew.heading: Build your template from scratch
templateNew.intro: After creating it you go straight to the editor. Add the available sections, reorder them by dragging, adjust colors, fonts, images and the intro, then press Save.
templateNew.reviewData: Check the messages under the fields and try again.
templateNew.slugHelp: It is generated automatically if left empty.

fonts.title: Font library
fonts.subtitle: Upload a font once and it appears as an option in every text property in the editor.
fonts.activeNote: An active font appears automatically in the font lists of the invitation and template editors.
fonts.none: The library is empty — upload the first font from the side.
fonts.addNote: You can upload TTF, OTF, WOFF or WOFF2, or paste a direct link to the font file.
fonts.familyHelp: Write the family name as it will appear in CSS, e.g. MyFont.
fonts.externalUrlHelp: Optional — use it instead of uploading the file.
fonts.footnote: The family name must match the font's internal name, e.g. Cairo or MyFont. Maximum file size is 8 MB.
fonts.added: Added the font “{{name}}” to the library.
fonts.reviewData: Check the data — upload a valid file or paste a direct link.
fonts.confirmDelete: Remove the font “{{name}}” from the library?
fonts.deleted: Removed the font “{{name}}” from the library.

music.title: Music library
music.how: Upload the track here once and you'll find it in the editor under Settings ← Music, ready to pick in any new invitation without uploading it again. Browsers usually block autoplay, so the guest presses play themselves.
music.none: The library is empty — upload the first track from the side.
music.externalUrlHelp: An alternative to uploading — a direct link to an audio file.
music.footnote: Maximum 8 MB. MP3 at 128 kbps is recommended — the difference isn't audible on a phone speaker and the file downloads much faster.
music.reviewData: Check the data — a field is missing.

dedupe.hint: Removes duplicate copies (same name and same content), keeping one of each track
dedupe.none: No real duplicates — some names match but the audio differs, so I left them alone.
dedupe.confirm: {{remove}} duplicate tracks will be deleted, keeping one copy of each track ({{keep}}). Any invitation or template using a deleted copy is switched to the kept one automatically. This can't be undone.
dedupe.doneDocs: {{docs}} documents were switched to the kept copy.

videos.title: Video library
videos.how: Upload any video here once and you'll find it in the editor when you pick a video and choose From the video library. If a video works as an intro, press Move to intros and it disappears from here and stays only in the intro library.
videos.howNote: The video is compressed automatically on upload (720p) and the audio is kept.
videos.none: The library is empty — upload the first video from the side.
videos.confirmMove: Move “{{name}}” to the intro library? It will disappear from the videos.

intros.title: Intro library
intros.how: Upload the video here once and you'll find it in the editor under Settings ← Intro ← Intro video, ready to pick in any invitation without uploading it again — just like the music library.
intros.howNote: The video is compressed automatically on upload (720p) and the audio is kept. Keep it short — 3 to 7 seconds is enough; the guest is waiting for the invitation, not a film.
intros.none: The library is empty — upload the first video from the side.
intros.externalUrlHelp: An alternative to uploading — a direct link to a video file.
intros.footnote: Maximum 8 MB. The cover image shows immediately before the video loads — it makes a big difference on mobile data.
intros.reviewData: Check the data — a field is missing.

plans.title: Plans and add-ons
plans.how: An add-on is an extra price on top of the plan, shown to the customer in the order form under the plan choice. If you give it a feature key (like music), buying it unlocks that feature in the invitation automatically even if the plan doesn't include it. Leave it empty if the add-on is a service, not a feature — like “24-hour delivery”.
plans.noAddons: No add-ons yet — add the first one from the side.
plans.plansNote: Name and price are edited right here. Features, bullets and colors are in “Full edit” — add-ons are added on top of the plan, they don't replace it.
plans.codeHelp: Optional — a feature key in the engine (music / rsvp / gallery …). If set, buying the add-on unlocks the feature in the invitation.
plans.descriptionPlaceholder: A line explaining the add-on to the customer
plans.reviewData: Check the data — a field is missing or wrong.
plans.soldDeactivated: “{{name}}” was bought in earlier orders, so it was hidden instead of deleted to keep old orders readable.

site.title: Site settings
site.warningTitle: The bar is on — but not visible
site.warningBody: There is no WhatsApp number or Facebook link, so the bar would be text without a button — and the page hides it entirely. Fill in one of them below and save, and it shows up right away in any template preview.
site.barBody: It appears at the bottom of the template preview only — not in a client invitation. The visitor taps WhatsApp and you receive a ready message with the name of the template they're looking at, so they don't need to describe anything.
site.homeTemplatesPerRowHelp: Only affects the templates section of the home page on phones — desktop and tablet stay the same.

fields.plansPublic: Show plans and prices on the site
fields.ordersEnabled: “Order your invitation” form on the site
fields.whatsappFloatEnabled: Floating WhatsApp button on the site

site.whatsappCtaMessageHelp: The ready message typed for the visitor when they tap the icon. It's different from the “Like the template?” bar message, which contains {template}.
site.whatsappMessageHelp: {template} is replaced with the name of the template the visitor is viewing.
site.tryBody: Open a template preview and see the bar at the bottom:
site.noSample: There are no visible templates to try it on.

state.enabledHidden: enabled but hidden — no contact method
state.offOrNoNumber: off or the number is empty
state.offOrEmpty: off or the link is empty
state.closed: closed — the buttons point to WhatsApp
state.floatHidden: enabled but hidden — the number is empty

site.footnote: If both are off the bar doesn't show at all — a bar without buttons is just noise.
